title: drawspec document, version 1
description: A declarative diagram. The author describes what the diagram means; every decision that requires seeing the output — coordinates, type size, colour, arrow-head geometry, z-order — is taken by drawspec and has no field here. Referential rules (node ids are unique; an edge names nodes that exist) are beyond JSON Schema and are enforced by `drawspec validate`, as are the readability budget (the most entries each kind may hold) and the cap of 2 elements with the 'emphasis' role (docs/format.md).

Drawn outside the drawing; the theme's `[canvas] caption` says above or below. Use a `note` for something attached to one element.

nodes.description: The boxes. Order is not a coordinate — the layout decides where a box goes — but it is the order siblings are drawn in: where nothing else separates two boxes of the same rank, they read in the order written here.

edges.description: What connects to what. A `tree` takes one edge per child.

groups.description: Boxes drawn around sets of nodes, each with its own caption.

bands.description: Named things that run alongside a set of boxes rather than containing them — drawn as a labelled bar beside the boxes they accompany. For the activity that goes on throughout: a source sheet with one continuous concern above its steps and another below says the steps are *surrounded* by them, and two such bands are peers. A `group` cannot say that — a box sits inside one container or none, so two groups over the same members had to be nested, which draws a hierarchy that is not there.

loops.description: The feedback loops of a causal loop diagram, each named and marked R (reinforcing) or B (balancing) inside the loop it closes — the type derived from the signs, never chosen. Needs `polarity` on the edges.

hub.description: What the loop turns around: the system a quality cycle improves, the model a data flywheel retrains. Not a step — it is drawn in the middle of the ring, outside the check that the ring closes through every node. An edge may join it to a step only as a spoke, in the roles 'aside', 'weak', 'link': a solid arrow to the middle would read as one more step. Needs a ring of at least 3 steps.

rise.description: Whether the series ascends: each entry drawn taller than the one before it, all sitting on a common baseline — the canvas floor for `columns`, the axis itself for `timeline`. For a scale where the order is the content and not merely the reading direction — five levels of open data, three degrees of a change — and where equal entries say they are peers, which is the opposite. The author says the series rises; the theme's `[box] rise` says by how much, so there is no per-column height to get wrong. Not a `pyramid`: that draws the last level as the *narrowest*, which is the right shape for a maturity model and the wrong one for a ladder.

spans.description: Named intervals between two entries, drawn as bars under the axis. For the quantity that is not a thing on the diagram but the distance between two things on it: a recovery objective is not an event, it is how much lies between the last backup and the disaster.

cells.description: What is in the grid. A cell states where it starts, not where it is drawn.

columns.description: Column headings, left to right. Omit for a matrix with none.

edges.description: What connects to what, between cells that carry an `id`. The cells of a grid are not always only cells: one may produce another, or come before it. The grid places them; the relations are a separate thing, and without them a reader sees a table where the source drew a process.

scale.description: Says the groups are **ordered**, and in what order: 2 to 5 group names, **weakest first** — `["rare", "sometimes", "often"]`. For a heatmap, a risk matrix, a skills matrix: a grid whose cells say *how much*. The cells are then filled by tone, light to dark, from the theme's `[mark] ramp` instead of with unrelated patterns, and the key lists every step in this order (with `key` texts where given). Every cell `group` must be one of these; a cell with no `group` stays blank, for *not assessed*. Names, not numbers: the author buckets the values.

key.description: What each group of cells is called, for the key drawn under the grid. Without one, a group is announced to the reader under the name the cells use for it — which is fine when that name is a name, and is how an id-shaped key like `carrega` ends up as visible text.

states.description: The conditions the machine can be in. A newline in `text` is a lead and a detail, as everywhere: the state's name over what holds in it. Every state must be reachable from `initial`.

initial.description: The state the machine starts in, drawn as a filled dot with an arrow to it. Required: reachability is measured from here. May name a group, which must then say its own `initial`.

final.description: The states the machine ends in, each drawn with an arrow to a ringed dot. A final state has no outgoing transition.

transitions.description: What moves the machine from one state to another, each labelled `event [guard] / action` from its own fields.

groups.description: Composite states: a frame around the states inside it, named at its corner. Groups may nest. A transition from a group leaves it from any state inside; one to a group enters it at the group's `initial`.

participants.description: Who takes part, drawn left to right in the order written, each a head with a dashed lifeline under it. The order is the reading order, not a coordinate. Every participant must send or receive a message.

messages.description: What is said, drawn top to bottom in the order written: the order is the diagram. A call (`flow`) answered later by a `weak` reply opens an activation bar on the receiver from the call's row to the reply's; nobody writes how tall it is.

fragments.description: Frames round a run of messages, `from` to `to`, and every participant they touch. Fragments nest or are apart; one that starts inside another and ends outside it is refused.

groups.description: A frame round a run of neighbouring lifelines, named at its top — *inside our account*. Members must be next to each other in `participants`, and a participant is in one group or none.

theme.description: A bundled theme name or the path of a theme file. A relative path is read from the document's own folder when the file is there, so a theme can sit beside the diagrams that use it.

nodes.description: Where the quantity starts, passes and ends. A node's column is derived from the flows — sources left, ends right — never written; the written order is where the order down each column starts.

flows.description: How much goes from one node to another, each a band whose thickness is in proportion to its `amount`. What reaches a node in the middle must all leave it, and nothing flows back.

unit.description: What the amounts are in — `tickets`, `cores`, `€ million` — written after each total.

values.description: Whether to write each node's total under its name. Defaults to true.

horizontal.description: The axis across, read as a measurement — unlike `quadrant`'s.

vertical.description: The axis up, read as a measurement — unlike `quadrant`'s.

label.description: Required: an unlabelled axis cannot be read.

unit.description: What the numbers are in, written after the label.

min.description: Where the axis starts. Omit to take it from the data.

max.description: Where the axis ends. Omit to take it from the data.

categories.description: Names for the positions 1, 2, 3 … along this axis, instead of numbers. What a bar chart's horizontal axis usually is: the quarters, the service models, the teams.

unit.description: What the numbers are in, written after the label.

min.description: Where the plan starts. Omit to take it from the tasks.

max.description: Where the plan ends. Omit to take it from the tasks.

categories.description: Names for the periods, in order, instead of numbers — months, sprints, quarters. The first period runs from 1 to 2, the second from 2 to 3, so a task over the first three is `start` 1, `end` 4. Sets the range itself, so not with `min` or `max`.

min.description: Where the scale starts, at the left arrowhead's side.

max.description: Where the scale ends: more than `min`.

step.description: The distance between two ticks, each labelled with its number. Omit it for a step a reader can count in, chosen from the range.

label.description: What the numbers measure, centred under them: `pH`, `Temperature`.

unit.description: What the numbers are in, written after the label: `°C`, `cm`.

ends.description: Two words for the low and the high end — `past` and `future`, `fully remote` and `fully on site` — written under the arrowheads, for a scale that is named rather than measured. No numbers are drawn: only the order and the gaps count, so not with `step` or `unit`.

text.description: The words themselves. May carry inline spans — `code` for the monospace role and **bold** for emphasis — because those are semantic, not typographic. A newline says this label is a lead and a detail rather than one sentence; the theme's `[box] lead` decides what the first paragraph looks like. Prefer it to punctuating the two apart inside one line.

members.description: The ids of the nodes this band accompanies. Unlike a group's, they are a set rather than a container: a band names something that runs alongside those boxes, and the same box may be under any number of bands.

id.description: What a brace's `over` names, for a brace over the whole bar. Unique among the bars and the parts.

over.description: What the brace spans: the ids of side-by-side parts of one bar, drawn over it (under it, for the last of several bars), or of whole bars — one bar the same way, several consecutive bars with an upright brace at their right.

amount.description: What the stretch adds up to. Checked: the parts' amounts must sum to it, and with units every brace must make one unit worth the same. Written unless `text` is given.

text.description: The words themselves. May carry inline spans — `code` for the monospace role and **bold** for emphasis — because those are semantic, not typographic. amount.description: How much the part is, more than 0: its length is in proportion, and its words default to the number. Give it even for the unknown — the `?` is its `text`.

units.description: How many equal boxes the part is, each one unit long: groups to multiply, the shares of a ratio, the fifths of a fraction. Not with `amount`, and not in a document whose parts have amounts.

text.description: The words themselves. May carry inline spans — `code` for the monospace role and **bold** for emphasis — because those are semantic, not typographic. polarity.description: A causal link's sign: more of the source means more (`+`) or less (`-`) of the target, written as the edge's label (`s`/`o` under a theme that says so). Every `flow` or `strong` edge of the document has one, or none does. **Only a `flow`.**

operations.description: What a class can do — `area() → float` — drawn in a compartment of their own under the fields. Strings, not objects: an operation is read, never linked to.

path.description: Where this sits, from the top of the tree: `src/app/main.py`. The folders it passes through are drawn without being listed. A trailing `/` makes it a folder — needed only for one with nothing listed inside. A last segment of `...` is a row standing for entries not listed.

note.description: A short comment drawn after the name, in the smaller label type.

link.description: Makes this entry a symbolic link, drawn with an arrow to this target. Written, never followed: the target need not be in the tree.

status.description: What a change did to this entry, as a diff would say it. Drawn as a labelled mark after the name — never as a colour alone.

id.description: Only needed for a relation to land on this row (`from_field`, `to_field`). Unique among the fields of the document.

text.description: The field's name, one line. `...` as the last field is a row standing for the fields not shown.

type.description: Its type — `uuid`, `float` — drawn right-aligned in the monospace face.

key.description: Whether it is a key, drawn as letters before the name — `PK`, `FK`, `UQ`: a word, never a colour.

operator.description: What the frame says about the messages inside it, written in its tab: `loop` repeats them, `opt` may happen, `alt` is one branch of several, `par` runs its branches at once.

to.description: The id of the last message inside the frame — the same as `from` for a frame round one message. Not before `from`.

text.description: The condition, beside the tab: what the loop runs over, when the option or the first branch happens. Written plainly; drawspec adds the brackets.

else.description: For `alt` and `par` only: where the frame is divided, each a dashed line above a message inside it, with that branch's condition under it.

Ranked instead, the middle object becomes just another row.

role.description: The semantic role, which the theme resolves to an appearance. Defaults to 'step'.

actor.description: Who performs this step — free text, and orthogonal to `role`. `role` says what kind of step it is; this says whose it is, and the two are independent: a human step can be routine and an automated one can be the critical path. Drawn as the box's **lead**, the name over what belongs to it, so the same words sit in the same place in every box and a reader can scan a column of them. Free text rather than an enum on purpose: an actor is told apart by its **name**, which is legible in greyscale and in any medium, so it costs none of the four non-colour channels the roles are told apart by. **Only a `flow`, a `tree` or a `cycle` draws one**, and a node that names an actor may not also write its own lead — the box has one lead and this is it.

note.description: A short aside attached to this element. **Only `timeline` draws one** — it goes under the axis, beside the entry's own mark.
